title: Add register_render(): evaluate rendered code chunks on daemons
description:
`register_render()` registers mirai as the evaluation executor for knitr and litedown chunk routing.

After `daemons(1, cleanup = FALSE)` and one call to `register_render()` (typically in a setup chunk), chunks tagged with `#| compute: gpu` evaluate on a daemon of the `"gpu"` compute profile instead of in the host session. Renderers own all option mapping and post-processing; mirai owns only execution.

`render_executor()` runs a function call synchronously on a daemon of the named profile and returns the value, or raises: daemon-side errors are re-raised with their original condition class and call, and infrastructure failures surface as readable `nng_error()` text.

Two per-profile checks run once per registration:
- a namespace probe errors informatively when a daemon lacks the renderer package (which otherwise fails opaquely as `could not find function`)
- a single-daemon check warns when a routed profile has more than one daemon, since cross-chunk state requires exactly one.

Renderer support is detected by feature (presence of the renderer's worker half), not version numbers, so this branch is testable against the renderer PRs.

Adds a `v08` vignette covering setup, state persistence, figures, and requirements.

CRAN release order is litedown & knitr → mirai.

title: Ignore non-cli arguments in `.progress` named lists
description:
Fixes #667. Also fixes the downstream purrr bug tidyverse/purrr#1253.

A named-list `.progress` option is now matched against the arguments of `cli::cli_progress_bar()` before use. 

Elements that do not match, such as `caller` added by purrr, are ignored instead of erroring. The same applies to `total`, `current`, `auto_terminate` and `.envir`, which mirai sets itself — these previously failed with "matched by multiple actual arguments".

title: Fix `.progress` bar leaking `envir` and closing caller's cli bar
description:
Closes #665.

The `.progress` collection option had two scoping faults:

- `envir <<-` assigned to the global environment, not the collection frame, so each collection left an `envir` variable in the user's global environment.
- mirai created its bar in the calling frame, which closed any cli progress bar already open there (cli permits one current bar per environment).

The fix removes the child environment and sets `current = FALSE` when creating the bar. The bar no longer registers as current, so it cannot close the caller's bar. Updates use the bar id, so ticking is unaffected.

title: Fix uninformative collection errors for non-mirai errorValues
description:
`stop_m()` read a `message` attribute that only a 'miraiError' carries, so `.stop` / `.flat` collection of a cancelled, timed-out, or connection-reset task raised a bare "In index: 1." with cli, and an entirely empty message without it.

The message is now derived by error kind: the message attribute for a 'miraiError' as before, `nng_error()` for integer 'errorValue's (which includes the code, e.g. "20 | Operation canceled"), and "Interrupted" for a 'miraiInterrupt'. The cli branch gains a proper `errorCondition()` parent so the cause is reported in the chain. All changes are on the terminal error path, so there is no impact on collection hot paths.

The test forces the base branch via `cli_enabled` to stay meaningful on runners with cli but not rlang, and matches "In index", which the pre-fix empty message fails.

Closes #642.

title: Remove ineffective promise cache from as.promise.mirai_map
description:
The memoization in `as.promise.mirai_map()` has never functioned: a 'mirai_map' is a plain list, so `attr(x, "promise") <-` triggers copy-on-modify and sets the attribute on a function-local duplicate that is discarded on return. Every call has therefore always built a fresh `promise_all()`, and nothing else reads the attribute.

This makes the method the one-liner it has always effectively been. No behavioural change: the per-element promises carry the real caching (mirai are environments, so that cache does persist), and repeated conversions of the same map produce equivalent promises over those shared element promises — verified identical resolution before and after. Existing promises tests cover the method, so no new test is added.

title: Fix .flat ignoring an errorValue in the first map element
description:
The `.flat` collection option only checked `is_error_value()` from the second element onwards, so a failed single-element map returned the miraiError silently as the flattened value, and a failure in the first element of a longer map surfaced as a misleading "differing type" error.

The error check now applies to every collected element. The expression is also restructured so that the first-element special case is folded into the type comparison: `typ` initializes to `FALSE`, which never equals a `typeof()` string, so index 1 enters the mismatch branch naturally and `i == 1L` is only evaluated there — keeping the per-element hot path at two checks.

Closes #639.

title: Fix daemon() exit code when walltime elapses while idle
description:
A recv timeout in the daemon loop was always attributed to idletime, so a daemon whose `walltime` elapsed while idle exited with code 1 rather than 2 — even when `idletime` was never set. The timeout is now attributed to walltime when the deadline has passed, mirroring the existing precedence where the higher code wins when multiple limits are exceeded. Tested in-process against a local listener, so the asserts depend only on timers never firing early, not on any completion window.

A second commit makes the #633 regression test robust under load: the timed-out case now degrades to a skip per the suite's `is_error_value` guard convention, while a connection reset (the original crash) remains a hard failure.

Closes #637.

title: Fix race_mirai() for profiles set with url and dispatcher = FALSE
description:
`create_sock()` was the one profile constructor not setting a `cv` on the profile environment, so for these profiles `race_mirai()` called `race_aio()` with a NULL cv, which degrades silently to returning `0L` without waiting.

Creating the cv in `create_sock()` makes it a true profile invariant: requests on these profiles now signal it on completion, so `race_mirai()` waits and returns the correct index. Synchronous compute profiles share this path and gain working `race_mirai()` too.

Closes #635.

title: Fix daemon crash for errors raised before evaluation begins
description:
If an error occurred before the eval frame existed, such as when assignment of `...` globals into the daemon's global environment failed, `mk_mirai_error()` found no eval frame on the stack and itself errored while extracting the stack trace. This secondary error escaped `daemon()`, killing the daemon process, with the host receiving an errorValue 19 rather than a miraiError.

The stack trace is now only trimmed and attached when the eval frame is found, so such errors return a regular miraiError (message intact, no stack trace) and the daemon survives to take the next task.

Closes #633.

title: Snapshot options by value for daemon cleanup
description:
`snapshot()` stored `.Options` directly, but that is the live options object which `options()` modifies in place, so the saved state tracked every subsequent change and the cleanup restore was a no-op. Snapshotting `as.list(.Options)` takes a real copy, at a cost of ~1µs at daemon startup.

Closes #631.

title: Threaded dispatcher with backpressure support
description:
Closes #454. Closes #581.

## Summary

- **Dispatcher moves from a separate R process to an in-process thread** (#581). The dispatcher logic, already reimplemented in C (nanonext 1.8.0), now runs as a thread within the host process. This eliminates inter-process communication overhead for dispatching and status queries, using `inproc://` transport instead of IPC sockets. `info()` reads dispatcher state directly rather than sending a query-response round trip.

- **New `capacity` argument for `daemons()`** (#454). Sets the maximum number of tasks (queued + executing) at the dispatcher. When the limit is reached, `mirai()` blocks until an existing task completes, providing backpressure to prevent unbounded memory growth. `NULL` (default) preserves existing unlimited queuing behavior.

## Benefits

- Lower dispatch overhead by eliminating the separate process and IPC round trips
- Direct memory access for `info()` instead of send/recv query protocol
- Backpressure prevents unbounded memory growth when producers outpace consumers (ML dataloaders, DB write pipelines, Shiny promise chains)
- Simpler startup: no `system2()` call to spawn a dispatcher process, no multi-step synchronization handshake
- Removes the exported `dispatcher()` function and `R/dispatcher.R` — net deletion of ~80 lines

fyi @lionel- this is a significant milestone for mirai

title: Add `try_mirai()` for non-blocking submission
description:
Closes #594.

When `daemons()` is configured with a `capacity` budget and the queue fills up, `mirai()` blocks the host R thread on the dispatcher gate until the queue drains. That's exactly what you want from a synchronous script — backpressure and bounded host memory — but it's the wrong default inside an event loop.

In Shiny, blocking the R thread freezes the UI, including unrelated reactivity and other sessions. Inside a `promises::then()` chain running under `later::run_now()`, it starves the loop. Anyone who'd rather drop, retry, or fan out to a different compute profile has no way to express that today — once `capacity` is set, every full queue is a blocking wait.

`try_mirai()` is the escape hatch. Same arguments as `mirai()`, same return type when there's room — but if the queue is at capacity, it returns `NULL` (invisibly) right away instead of blocking, and the caller can handle this as desired.

Where there's no gate to consult (no dispatcher, or `capacity` unset), it always returns a mirai — the contract is "don't block on queue pressure". `mirai()`'s signature and behaviour are unchanged, so existing scripts keep working exactly as before.

The new failure mode lives in the function name, mirroring Tokio's `try_send` / `send` split.

@wlandau fyi you can proceed with testing once this is merged.

title: Ability to pass config options in `http_config()` for Posit Workbench
description:
Builds on `http_config()` from mirai 2.6 to make scaling daemons across a Posit Workbench Launcher backend (e.g. Kubernetes) straightforward. Customisation lives on `http_config()` itself rather than a new exported function.

## Key changes

- `http_config()` accepts `...` forwarded to `data` when it is a function.
- The default Posit Workbench `data` builder gains `cluster`, `resource_profile`, `cpus`, `memory`, `job_name` and `rscript` options.
- Usage: `http_config(cluster = "Kubernetes", resource_profile = "rstudio")` or `http_config(cluster = "Kubernetes", cpus = 4, memory = 8192)`.
- Reference vignette and `?http_config` updated; mocked tests cover the new options (R/launchers.R coverage 100%).

title: Switch `capacity` from task count to memory budget (MB)
description:
Closes #589.

`capacity` now sets a memory budget (MB, metric — 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes) over queued task payloads at dispatcher, rather than a count of inflight tasks. Memory is the resource that actually puts the host at risk of OOM; a task count is a poor proxy when payload sizes vary by orders of magnitude.

- `NULL` (default) is unbounded; degenerate values (0, non-finite, negative) also degrade to unbounded.
- New `dispatcher_capacity()` returns `c(used, peak, capacity)` in MB for monitoring queue pressure against the budget.
- Gate is skipped on the hot path when `capacity = NULL`, so the default pays no per-task cost.

Requires the corresponding nanonext changes (byte-based gate, `.dispatcher_capacity` accessor).

title: HTTP launcher concept
description:
Closes #552.

Implements `http_config()` for HTTP-based remote daemon launching.

## Summary           
             
  - Adds `http_config()` for launching remote daemons via HTTP APIs           
  - Provides zero-config defaults for Posit Workbench, with full customization for arbitrary HTTP endpoints                                
  - Supports flexible authentication via session cookies and/or bearer tokens                                                   

## Details
                                          
`http_config()` creates a remote configuration that launches daemons by making HTTP POST requests to an API endpoint. This enables integration with platforms that expose job launch APIs.                               

Posit Workbench (zero-config):
```r                                 
# Just works when running inside Posit Workbench
daemons(n = 4, url = host_url(), remote = http_config())
```
The defaults automatically:
  - Discover the Workbench API URL and session cookie
  - Query the compute environment to determine cluster, container image, and resource profile
  - Configure `.libPaths()` to match the current session

Custom HTTP endpoints:
```r 
http_config(                                                              
  url = "https://api.example.com/launch",                                 
  method = "POST",                                                        
  cookie = function() Sys.getenv("MY_SESSION_COOKIE"),                    
  token = function() Sys.getenv("MY_API_KEY"),                            
  data = '{"command": "%s"}'                                              
)                                                        
```                                                                     
The `data` parameter should include a %s placeholder where the `mirai::daemon()` call will be inserted.

The R system is less than ideal as it does not allow for synchronization, nor does it use atomics. But as it is all we have, we have to be a bit more hands-on than we'd like.

It is also the only way to interrupt running arbitrary user-supplied code that we have no control over, otherwise a cooperative approach would be much preferred.

title: Synchronous compute profiles
description:
Closes #435. For evaluating mirai in the current process. Enables use of `browser()` for interactive debugging.

```r
library(mirai)
daemons(sync = TRUE)
m <- mirai(
  {
    browser()
  },
  .args = list(x = 1)
)
daemons(0)
```

Would drop us into a browser instance with access to `x`.

Each mirai is evaluated separately so it works for `mirai_map()` etc. regardless of the number of evaluations.

``` r
library(mirai)
daemons(sync = TRUE, .compute = "sync")
with_daemons("sync", {
  mp <- mirai_map(1:3, \(x) Sys.getpid())
})
daemons(0, .compute = "sync")
mp[]
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 32155
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 32155
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] 32155
```

```r
daemons(6)
#> [1] 6
nextget("dispatcher")
#> [1] "ipc:///tmp/9a21b5f73cf632e95535ce78"
```

```r
library(mirai)
daemons(url = "ipc:///tmp/9a21b5f73cf632e95535ce78")
#> [1] 0
```
You can then submit mirai from either R session to the same pool of [6] daemons.

1. This is enabled automatically - you create daemons in the usual way (no need to expressly create a pool)
2. Other sessions can 'attach' to a pool simply by providing the dispatcher socket address to `url` of `daemons()`

title: Simplify SSH Tunnelling for Distributed Computing
description:
### Background

SSH tunnelling support is currently somewhat buried away within `ssh_config()`.

For `ssh_config()`:
 - currently `port` is only applicable if `tunnel = TRUE`.
 - it is not immediately obvious that `port` refers to the tunnel port, and not the SSH port for instance.

### Solution

This PR attempts a radical overhaul to make distributed computing over SSH tunnelling more intuitive and easy to use.

`ssh_config()` :
- now only records a tunnel flag, and not the port, hence the `port` argument is completely removed
- the tunnel port is determined dynamically by the launcher
- this allows specification of `tcp://127.0.0.1:0` to automatically assign a free port at `daemons()`

`local_url()`:
- gains logical argument 'tcp' to automatically provide the necessary URL for SSH tunnelling
- gains argument 'port' to specify a specific port if desired

This means that launching daemons via SSH tunnelling is now just a one-liner:
```r
daemons(n = 4, url = local_url(tcp = TRUE), remote = ssh_config("ssh://10.75.32.90", tunnel = TRUE))
```

title: Remove daemons() implicit behaviour
description:
Multiple calls to e.g. `daemons(1)` will implicitly reset daemons before re-launching them. This was introduced in mirai 1.3.0.

Before then, subsequent calls would return the same integer value but not actually do anything.  The could be confusing and non-obvious. The current behaviour was thought to be an improvement on this by acting on any (explicit) call to `daemons()`.

However this creates more implicit behaviour by resetting daemons before re-launching them, and can cause ongoing mirai to resolve to 'errorValues'. Although this is documented, it is nevertheless undesirable.

Now subsequent calls to `daemons()` will simply error with an informative message. An explicit `daemons(0)` reset is now required prior to creating new daemons settings.

With mirai 2.0, as you can now add or remove daemons without limit even with dispatcher, there is even less of a need to revise daemons settings. For local use, if you start with `daemons(2)`, you can increase that to 4 simply by `launch_local(2)`. It should be the case that `daemons()` only need to be called once (for each compute profile).

title: New hybrid dispatcher concept (enables mirai cancellation)
description:
**New default dispatcher**

Inviting @jcheng5 @hadley for review and comment.

This is a complete re-design of dispatcher using a more optimal and future-proof architecture.

The key difference is that whereas previously dispatcher used one socket *per* daemon connection, it now uses one socket for *all* daemon connections.

The previous configuration was necessary due to limitations of the NNG req/rep (PRC) protocol using a round-robin algorithm. This is typically optimal behaviour for web servers and similar applications, but not for arbitrary execution where evaluation times may vary greatly.

The novel solution is to preserve the req/rep abstraction for the user, with `mirai()` working substantially the same way, but to re-wire the dispatcher / daemon back-end to use an alternative protocol (NNG's pair 1 poly). This allows one-to-many mapping with directed sends, which is exactly what's needed to implement an optimal task queue dispatcher.

**Mirai Cancellation**

Allows actual cancellation of mirai when using `stop_mirai()`, as per the below example:
- `stop_mirai()` returns `TRUE` if the task is awaiting execution - it is discarded from the queue. Cancellation is certain.
- `stop_mirai()` returns `NA` if the task was in-execution. An interrupt is sent to the daemon process, but it may have been partially executed by this point.
- `stop_mirai()` returns `FALSE` if the task has already completed or been cancelled.

``` r
library(mirai)
daemons(2, output = TRUE)
#> [1] 2
m1 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 1 done")})
m2 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 2 done")})
m3 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 3 done")})
Sys.sleep(0.1)
(stop_mirai(m3))
#> [1] TRUE
(stop_mirai(m2))
#> [1] NA
(stop_mirai(m2))
#> [1] FALSE
#> [1] "mirai 1 done"
```
<sup>Created on 2024-12-01 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

**Other notable improvements**

- Only one (IPC) socket connection from host to dispatcher (previously there was an additional control socket for sending information requests).
- For distributed computing, plain TCP connections can be used without the added overhead of the websocket layer, as only one URL is required no matter how many daemons. We also don't need to manage many URLs and ensure a one-to-one mapping of each.
- Connection changes tracked efficiently and accurately (due to upgrades at `nanonext`) hence retiring a lot of custom code that was designed to deal with this.
- Connected daemons can be scaled up and down freely without limit (we had to set a maximum before).
- More succinct and intuitive status summary, for example (borrowing the above example):

``` r
library(mirai)
daemons(2, output = TRUE)
#> [1] 2
m1 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 1 done")})
m2 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 2 done")})
m3 <- mirai({Sys.sleep(1); print("mirai 3 done")})
Sys.sleep(0.1)
status()
#> $connections
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $daemons
#> [1] "abstract://595b781203f9cad1ea0f39f8"
#> 
#> $mirai
#>  awaiting executing completed 
#>         1         2         0
```

<sup>Created on 2024-12-01 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Use R's temporary directory for local Unix sockets
description:
Local filesystem sockets currently default to `/tmp` on macOS and other non-Linux Unix systems. That can be outside the writable area in sandboxes with a private temporary directory.

Use `tempdir()` for these sockets, so `local_url()` and local daemon startup follow the temporary directory selected when R starts. Escape quotes in daemon URLs when generating R code, so quoted directory names also work for persistent and ephemeral workers.

The implementation updates the default IPC prefix and all three worker-command generators, with public-API regression coverage and documentation of the socket-path length limit. Linux's abstract sockets and Windows' named pipes retain their existing defaults.
